records.title: Bearframe runtime terrain tilesheet geometry
records.source: Founder-defined Bearframe World Editor v1 production standard
records.summary: World Editor v1 runtime tilesheets are 384 by 768 pixels using an 8 by 16 grid of 48 by 48 pixel tiles. Use top-left origin, exactly 128 slots, RGBA PNG, clean transparency, and no labels, gaps, or resizing. Preserve stable tile IDs and order.

records.title: Bearframe engine release gate
records.source: Founder instructions for Bearframe RPG engine completion
records.summary: Engine development is the priority before gameplay content. Preserve existing source and GitHub history. Include Android controller and touch input, save-load verification, inventory integration and automated checks; do not declare a broken feature fixed before reproducible tests or on-device evidence.

records.title: Ghost Grid and Echo Frame ancient deterioration canon
records.source: Founder-approved Bearframe RPG reference images and art-direction corrections, Nov 2026
records.summary: Ghost Grid constructs are ancient advanced machines with accumulated age, heavy wear, overgrowth, and mechanical faults. Echo Frames are distinct old Ghost Grid-era sentient Frames, often humanoid or hulking with layered armor, exposed systems, torn fabric, and individualized silhouettes. They are weathered and overgrown too, with conspicuous glitches, memory/display instability, actuator failures, and unpredictable motion. Character reference sheets for Fract, Relay, Ruin, Murmur, and Bastion guide appearance. Broken details must be intentional and readable, not shortcuts for poor sprite anatomy.

records.title: Anchored stance test for six-leg pixel-art rigs
records.source: Original 12-frame Pillow exercise and local automated checks (2026-11-10); Saint11 pixel-art tutorials https://saint11.org/blog/pixel-art-tutorials/ ; Bearframe Warehouse existing Palinode gait record
records.summary: In a 12-frame 160x112 RGBA Pillow mechanics exercise, six indexed legs were rendered with alternating tripod groups; each frame had exactly three stance legs, planted feet used fixed screen-space anchors while the body translated, and eight physical archive-ring panel markers changed position around a fixed pylon. Validation passed leg counts, stance counts, transparency and ring movement; this does NOT prove natural gait, anatomy, silhouette separation or canon fidelity. Earlier leg drills tested static hip anchors; this exercise changes to moving hips plus anchored stance contacts. Limitation: swing trajectories jump at wraparound, far-side legs overlap, ring is schematic. Reproduce using explicit phase=(frame/N + tripod_offset) mod 1, stance phase<0.5, and compare native 1x frames before approval.

records.title: Comprehensive Bearframe visual-art training checklist
records.source: Founder correction to Auren pixel-art study scope, Nov 2026
records.summary: Character design is ADDITIONAL homework, not a replacement for existing pixel-art work. Train and evaluate all competencies together: native-scale pixel placement and cluster discipline, clean contours, anatomy and proportions, distinctive and appealing character/portrait design, shape language, strong silhouettes, expressive face/visor/helmet design, readable armor and materials, lighting and color, frame-by-frame animation timing and movement weight, articulated mechanical geometry, natural accumulated overgrowth and age/damage, and intentional Ghost Grid mechanical faults versus distinctive Echo Frame glitch behavior. Compare original reference designs to native-resolution sprites and portraits; document failures, revisions, and objective QC before production approval. Previous rough assets are practice only, not finished.

records.title: Native pixel-art training and quality gate
records.source: Founder-requested study and corrections from Bearframe asset sessions
records.summary: Produce pixel art with actual raster or pixel editing tools, not an AI generated image as substitute. Evaluate at native resolution, check silhouettes, topology, consistent pixel size and every required limb, then compare passes before accepting a base animation frame.

records.title: Native scale and complete sprite anatomy
records.source: Founder feedback on previous Bearframe pixel-art attempts
records.summary: Evaluate sprites at native pixel resolution before enlarging them. Avoid blocky oversized pixels that obscure the silhouette. Check that full limb anatomy is present, including both legs where the design requires them. Review readability and proportions before treating a sprite as a locked base frame.

records.title: Palinode six leg gait evaluation
records.source: Bearframe pixel-art study assignment and prior exercise feedback
records.summary: Practice an articulated six-leg mechanical walking loop with distinct legs and alternating tripod support and swing phases. Check leg endpoints frame by frame, contact timing, silhouette and missing limb artifacts. Treat previous attempts as exercises, not finished production assets.

records.title: Relay portrait round 06 shape hierarchy lesson
records.summary: In a native 144x144 Relay portrait experiment, rebuilding the asymmetric torn hood, tilted CRT face, separated broken halo and scarf as large silhouette clusters before damage/detail improved reference identity compared with a prior symmetrical frontal round. Integer-pixel Pillow edits used 25 colors and binary alpha; validation confirms file structure, NOT artistic quality. Remaining weaknesses: overly rounded CRT, weak shoulder planes, thin overgrowth, and display-only glitches. Next practice: sharper 3/4 faceted CRT, stronger shoulder anatomy, organic seam growth, and true-motion studies.

records.title: Relay portrait Round 07 silhouette and perspective failure analysis
records.summary: Native 208x208 hand-authored Relay portrait study used 29-color palette and binary RGBA alpha; separate silhouette, faceted CRT/material, and sparse age passes; tested alternative broken-halo placements. Compared with Round 06, the CRT is more oblique and layer hierarchy clearer, but the silhouette still merges halo and hood near the top, shoulders remain shallow, and the design is not production quality. Technical PNG validation is not artistic validation. Next: three tiny monochrome thumbnail silhouettes, negative-space test at 1x, and focused 3/4 CRT/hood construction BEFORE lighting, overgrowth or glitches. Keep all prior animation and degeneration subjects in parallel.

records.title: Relay Round 08 silhouette separation versus character appeal
records.summary: Three native 104x128 integer-pixel silhouette studies compared broken relay-ring placement while holding Relay's body constant. A/B/C ring-to-body minimum gaps were 2.83/3.61/4.00 pixels with no direct overlap. B better isolates the left rim, C is top-heavy; these numerical tests check geometry but NOT artistic quality. A separate 112x100 angled CRT material-plane exercise was also completed. All designs still fail canonical character-art review because hood/head and shoulders remain generic/rounded; further angular asymmetrical silhouette and 3/4 perspective practice is required before effects or animation. Preserve this critical failure along with the evidence and continue the other study subjects.

records.title: Relay Round 6 portrait failure and art-method correction
records.source: Founder direct visual critique of Relay portrait Round 6, Nov 2026
records.summary: Founder quality feedback: the Relay Round 6 portrait resembles crude MS Paint drawing and is not a polished or sufficiently faithful Echo Frame design. Basic programmatic circles, polygons, flat fills, and added surface speckles are not a substitute for strong character-design fundamentals. Corrective workflow: study canonical Relay reference; establish an appealing, asymmetrical perspective-correct head and strong silhouette; build helmet/CRT display/hood and armor in meaningful layered planes; place and revise pixel clusters deliberately; verify visual fidelity at native resolution on light and dark backgrounds; only after the still image succeeds add wear, moss, corruption, or animation. Preserve all existing animation, overgrowth, silhouette and glitch training. Treat this pass as an unsuccessful quality-gate attempt and retain critique rather than celebrating minor metrics.

records.title: Evidence first warehouse learning loop
records.source: Atlas Warehouse operational policy and Founder requirement for continuous improvement
records.summary: Save reusable public-safe project techniques with source and review status. Do not promote a claim to tested without repeatable evidence. When an experiment fails, record the failure and correction. Retrieve exact records before taking action and preserve commit history.
